text: The append is one synchronous operation of rwb-decision on the decision base, POST /api/recovery/decision/v1/decision-log, called by rwb-agent as the first step of its transaction with the case reference, the source type and reference, the item key (the proposed code or the policy version), the decision code, the final call, the reason, the effective date, the recommendation, an idempotency key and the decided time, and answered 201 with the record reference, the chain sequence, the entry hash and the decided time; the agent version and the data date are read from the run and never from the caller. The request and answer field set of section 12.1 stays the placeholder until the contract baseline is agreed.
why: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 documents only the reads of the recommendation, the approvals and the ledger, and the legacy story writes the entry in process inside the monolith, so the write path of the target has neither a method nor a path nor a body, while rwb-agent has to store a decision reference on its feedback row and the whole action has to fail when the record cannot be written.
read: TSD P7 v2 T-A.1 (API-P7-002 to API-P7-008), T3.1 (decision_log_entry DF-DEC-001 to DF-DEC-031); FSD P7 v3 A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-04 and AC-EXC-P7-002-05; legacy RWB-E2-029 sections 4 steps 6 and 7, 5 X6, 12 and 13; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 41; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-03, DP-11 and DP-13
applied_in: Sections 1, 3, 4 steps 2 and 10, 5 X4 and X5, 7 AC1 and AC5 to AC7, 10, 11, 12.1, 12.8 and 13
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-agent (P10) and rwb-decision (P7) owners, in the baseline review of RWB-P10-E2029-CON and of this service's contract
impact: No business value changes: the code, the versions, the final calls, the reason and the chain are the legacy ones. If the append becomes an event or an in-process library call on the caller's side, one consumed or published row changes and the fail-closed behaviour of AC7 and the one-record rule of AC5 keep their criteria.

text: The promotion decision code is a value of LOV-DECISION read through the reference-data contract of rwb-case with the version in force, and the final calls APPROVED, RETURNED, REFUSED and REJECTED are rows of this service's final-call vocabulary in the same list; neither the code nor a final call is a constant in code. A code, a final call or a required version that is not of its list is refused with 422 and MSG-P7-009 naming the field, and the value of the promotion code itself is not invented here.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.2 carries no LOV-DECISION values and no final-call list, the legacy story gives no code for the promotion it records, and BR-P7-001 forbids a business value in code, so the record cannot be validated or tested without a stated reading of where the values live and which values they are.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-003 and DF-DEC-012) and T3.2; FSD P7 v3 A2.1.3.1 BR-P7-001, A2.2.4.3 AC-EXC-P7-002-05 and A2.7; legacy RWB-E2-029 sections 8 BR1 and BR6, 12 and 14; Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings (reference data to P3) and R5.5 DP-07
applied_in: Sections 3, 4 steps 4 and 7, 5 X1, 7 AC1 to AC3, 8 BR4 and BR7, 9, 12.1, 13 configuration and 14
confirm: Business analyst P7 with the reference-data owner of rwb-case, in the baseline review of LOV-DECISION and of the final-call list
impact: If the list names the promotion code differently, one reference row and one assertion of AC1 change; no table, contract or criterion of the record changes.

text: The decision of a rejected proposal is the proposed code X1 to X7 of LOV-DECISION and the final call is REJECTED, exactly as legacy AC4 writes the entry, so the code of a rejection is read from the list and never derived from the item key in code; a confirmation writes no record here at all, because the deviation and its record are rwb-deviation's on the S8 path.
why: The legacy story records 'decision X6' on a rejection and gives no decision code for a confirmation, and the target splits the two verdicts between this service and the deviation service, so which verdict writes an entry here has to be stated or the ledger would hold two records for one confirmation.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-029 sections 4 steps 6 to 8, 7 AC2 and AC4, 8 BR3 and BR4, and 12; TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (DF-DEC-003, DF-DEC-012, DF-DEC-013) and T3.2; Architecture v5 slide 13 (S8 row) and slide 41
applied_in: Sections 1, 4 step 10, 7 AC5 and AC9, 8 BR7, 9, 11 and 19
confirm: Business analyst P7 with the rwb-deviation (S8) owner and the rwb-agent (P10) owner, in the wave 2 walkthrough of the confirmation path
impact: If a confirmation also required an entry here, one more append call and one criterion are added and the S8 record would be the second; the rejection record and its reason do not change.

text: A policy promotion has no case, so its `approval` row is written with the source type AGENT_POLICY, the policy version as its source reference and the segment pair with the condition set in its terms; the case-less variant of the row, the value of the source-type column and the columns that carry the segment are read as the variant this story needs and are not treated as a new table. The `source_type` value AGENT_POLICY is assumed because no source enumerates that column.
why: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 makes `approval.case_id` required and gives no column for a segment or a condition set, while the legacy promotion is an administrative item with no case and the decision must still be routed to the level the delegation of authority names.
read: TSD P7 v2 T3.1 (approval DF-DEC-032 to DF-DEC-053, case_id required, source_type, source_ref, terms) and T3.2 (LOV-APPROVAL-STATUS, LOV-CAPABILITY, LOV-APPROVAL-LEVEL); FSD P7 v3 A2.4 and A2.7; legacy RWB-E2-029 sections 3, 4 step 3 and 10
applied_in: Sections 4 step 4, 7 AC1, 8 BR3 and BR5, 9, 11, 12.7 and 13
confirm: Data steward of rwb-decision with the solution architect, in the baseline review of the approval table
impact: If the table is widened instead, one migration step and one column list change; the routing, the statuses and the record do not.

text: The per-service database login of DP-02 is called the rwb-decision login in this story because no source gives its name; the Flyway user and the outbox relay identity are environment configuration of the platform and are not values of the story.
why: Template and Rules R4 requires one login per service and no source this story may read names it, so the story needs a phrase that is not the monolith login and does not invent an identifier.
read: Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 slides 8 and 41 (19 schemas, one login each); context pack P7 (schema rwb_decision)
confirm: Platform team and the ACE DB story owner at the schema review
impact: If the name differs, one configuration value and one phrase change; no criterion is affected.

text: The third event the Ownership Map gives P7, EV-30, is not published by this story: its name, its topic and its payload are not written in any source this story may read, and this story therefore publishes only the record event on the shared topic and the approval event on the service topic. EV-30 stays with the slice of the service that owns that subject.
why: Template and Rules R4 fixes the event naming rule but no source the WP allows names what EV-30 is, and a story may not invent an event name or a payload that another slice owns.
read: Context pack P7 (Events EV-08, EV-09, EV-30); TSD P7 v2 T5.3 (DecisionRecorded, ApprovalRequested); Template and Rules v1 R4 (event names rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1)
confirm: Solution architect P7 with the event catalogue owner, at the wave 2 event review
impact: If EV-30 is the approval event under another name, one row of section 12.3 is renamed and one assertion of AC1 changes; the outbox transaction does not.

text: The nine contracts the DP table adds and the two operations no pattern names are read as prerequisites of the capability and not as per-story blockers: the platform contracts of waves 0 and 1 (RWB-PLT-E1027-CON, RWB-PLT-E1042-CON, RWB-PLT-E1043-CON, RWB-PLT-TE006-CON and RWB-PLT-N001-CON) are held by every wave 1 service, the published contracts C RWB-P3-E1042-CON and C RWB-P3-E1043-CON, the P4 authorise call and the P1 freshness read are answered by their fakes until they are published, and the metadata rows keep None and RWB-P10-E2029-CON; the story stays Day 1 and no H dependency is added to a lane of depth one.
why: Template and Rules R5.5 adds a dependency per pattern and R5.7 rules 1 to 3 make a platform contract and a published contract of another service non-blocking, while the plan record must not be rewritten by a story and the dependencies must not disappear from the delivery map.
read: Template and Rules v1 sections R5.4, R5.5 (DP-03, DP-05, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-11, DP-13, DP-19) and R5.7; the story record of RWB-P7-E2029-APP in _work/msr/wp/B2-P7-002.md; Architecture v5 slides 14, 20, 41 and 44

text: This story has no feature switch of its own: the legacy flag rwb.agent.screening-l1 stays with RWB-P10-E2029-APP, it gates the mode and the panel there, and it never gates the record of a promotion or of a rejection, because a promotion that took effect or a verdict a person gave without its record is a defect and not a degraded mode; the mode SHADOW of a segment is a policy value of rwb-agent and not a switch of this service.
why: The legacy story sets one flag for the whole capability and the target splits the capability across three services, so the flag has to be placed, and placing it on the record path would let a configuration change create an unrecorded decision.
read: Legacy RWB-E2-029 section 13 (feature flag rwb.agent.screening-l1) and section 8 BR1 and BR2; Template and Rules v1 R3 default rulings (feature flags, platform library); Architecture v5 slide 20; FSD P7 v3 A2.5
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-agent owner and the platform library owner, in the baseline review of the flags
impact: If a flag is required on the record path it can only hide the approval item and never the record; the append, its transaction and every criterion stay unchanged.
